children: The opening game of the 2026-2027 NFL football season takes place on Wednesday night when the Seattle Seahawks host the New England Patriots. The American Gaming Association estimated that Americans will legally wager $29.5B on the 2026 NFL season through U.S.-regulated commercial sportsbooks. The estimate includes preseason games, futures booked as early as March, the playoffs, and Super Bowl LXI scheduled for February 2027. Of note, the forecast is essentially level with last year's state-regulated betting handle of $29.4B.

"Since the widespread launch of backdoor sports betting on so-called prediction markets, the growth of legal handle has stalled," highlighted AGA President and CEO Bill Miller. The prediction market platforms were highlighted as operating outside the regulatory frameworks governing sports betting in the 40 jurisdictions where it is legal, while also bypassing the laws prohibiting sports betting in the 11 states that have chosen not to legalize it.
Notably, sports bets constitute about 80% of Kalshi's
volume, which includes an estimated $5.1B in volume from users between the ages of 18 and 20, which is below the legal age in 35 of 40 jurisdictions where sports betting is legal.
For the 2026–27 season, the NFL has renewed and expanded its official commercial relationship with sportsbooks. The league announced multiyear agreements with DraftKings (
) have held official NFL betting relationships since 2021, while Fanatics (

) joins the group under the new arrangement. The partnerships provide brand and marketing rights, but they also signal that the league continues to treat licensed sportsbooks as its primary commercial betting category.
